simulate.title: Simulate
simulate.subtitle: Run SimulationCraft against a character to see expected DPS and per-ability damage breakdown. Paste your /simc string from in-game, pick fight profiles and talent loadouts, then compare.

talentFinder.title: One-Button Talent-Finder
talentFinder.intro: Pulls the top-1000 WCL logs for your fight profile and finds the strongest talent build for the Blizzard one-button macro (with the in-game 25% GCD penalty). Pick a search strategy below.
talentFinder.profileHint: Talents in this paste are ignored — the Talent-Finder substitutes its own candidate builds. Gear and stats are kept.
talentFinder.profileNotConfigured: No encounter mapped — ask an admin
talentFinder.thresholdHint: A talent slot counts as 'contested' when at least this fraction of the top-1000 disagree on it. Lower = more variants. Default 0.25. Ignored by the sweep strategy.
talentFinder.fixedRotation: Rotation is fixed to Blizzard one-button (one_button_mode=1).
talentFinder.errorEmptyProfile: Paste the full /simc text — looks too short.
talentFinder.errorProfileNotConfigured: No encounter is mapped to this fight profile. An admin needs to configure it first.
talentFinder.resultsHint: Top {shown} builds by mean DPS under one-button. Copy a build's Blizzard export code to use it in-game.
talentFinder.resultsWaiting: Waiting for the first runs to finish…
talentFinder.strategy_sweep_hint: Sims every distinct real build from the top-1000 under one-button, then refines the best one talent-by-talent. Most thorough — escapes the meta blind spot. Runtime ~20-45 min (longer for Mythic+).
talentFinder.strategy_cluster_hint: Only varies the talent slots the top-1000 disagree on. Quick first look, but blind to talents the whole meta agrees on. Runtime ~5-10 min.
talentFinder.runtimeNote: Heads up: the Talent-Finder runs hundreds of simulations — it is not instant. Estimated runtime for the selected strategy is shown above; you can leave the page and come back.
talentFinder.screeningHint: Each talent change vs the baseline ({baseline} DPS), measured under one-button. The combine round below explores the winners together.
talentFinder.progressQueued: Queued — waiting for a free simulation slot…
talentFinder.progressNote: This runs hundreds of simulations and takes a while. You can leave this page — it keeps going in the background.

simulate.sidecarUnreachable: SimC sidecar unreachable — ask an admin to start the simc service.
simulate.profileHint: Type /simc in-game, copy the whole block. Consumables and raid buffs are added automatically.

customModal.title: Custom fight profile
customModal.intro: Tweak how the encounter looks. Start from a preset and adjust from there.
customModal.fightStyleHint: Patchwerk = boss tank-and-spank with the number of targets you set; DungeonSlice = simc's built-in M+ wave sequence (own pacing); CastingPatchwerk = caster-friendly variant. Same options simc itself supports.
customModal.dungeonSliceNote: DungeonSlice has its own pre-defined wave sequence (boss + add waves over ~6 minutes). It ignores the 'Targets' setting entirely and uses its built-in pacing. For a 'X mobs for Y seconds' test, pick Patchwerk instead and set the number of targets there.
customModal.desiredTargetsHint: How many enemies are up. Council uses 3, small M+ trash ~4-6, big pulls 8-12.
customModal.desiredTargetsDisabledHint: Ignored by DungeonSlice — it uses its own wave sequence.
customModal.maxTimeHint: Encounter length. Raid bosses ~4 min, M+ trash pulls ~60 s, M+ bosses ~3 min, AoE burst test ~12 s.
customModal.targetErrorHint: Smart-sim stops once the DPS confidence interval drops below this percentage. 0.05 = tight, 0.1 = relaxed (faster).

simulate.rotationModesHint: Pick one or more. Each ticked mode is simulated against every loadout × fight profile, so adding 'Blizzard One-Button' gives you a direct with/without comparison.
simulate.queueHint: Sidecar busy: {running} running, {queued} ahead in queue. We'll start as soon as a slot opens.
simulate.queueWaitingForWorker: Waiting for a free worker slot…
simulate.loadoutsDetectedHint: {count} loadout(s) detected in your /simc profile. Tick the ones you want to compare (max {max}).
simulate.loadoutsNoneDetected: Paste a /simc profile above — we'll list the active talent build plus every saved loadout from the in-game UI so you can compare them.

rotationHint.simc_default: Uses SimC's community-maintained near-optimal rotation for this spec.
rotationHint.blizzard: Realistic one-button-macro simulation: Blizzard's Assisted Combat APL with the in-game 25% GCD penalty (one_button_mode=1) and cooldowns enabled.
rotationHint.custom: Runs whatever actions= block is in the pasted profile. Pick this only if you wrote a custom APL.

simulate.talentsHint: Paste talents= / class_talents= / spec_talents= lines to override what's in the profile. Leave empty to use the profile's talents.
simulate.iterationsHint: Default {def} (~2% error). Higher = more precise but slower.

adminSimc.title: SimulationCraft sidecar
adminSimc.hint: Pulls the latest simulationcraftorg/simc image (rebuilt daily with current binary + DBC data) and recreates the simc container. Requires ADMIN_DOCKER_CONTROL=true.
adminSimc.rebuildTitle: Rebuild simc from source (bleeding-edge game data)
adminSimc.rebuildHint: Pulls latest simc source + downloads fresh DBC files from the public WoW CDN + (optionally) layers a DBCache.bin from your local WoW client on top. Use when a WoW hotfix breaks talent strings before the upstream simc image catches up. Takes 10-20 min.
adminSimc.dbcacheHint: Optional: select DBCache.bin from <WoW>/Cache/ADB/<region>/DBCache.bin for the absolute latest hotfix data.

localAi.title: Local AI model (llama.cpp)
localAi.help: Switch the loaded GGUF, free disk space, and stop or start inference without touching docker-compose. Changes take effect after the model has finished downloading and llama-server has loaded it into VRAM (10–40 min on first download).
localAi.unreachable: Local-AI container is not running. Start it with `docker compose --profile local-ai up -d` or rebuild after pulling the latest changes.
localAi.startHint: Boot llama-server with the configured model
localAi.stopHint: Terminate llama-server (frees VRAM). Inference becomes unavailable until restarted.
localAi.noCachedModels: No GGUF files cached yet — Apply config to download.
localAi.deleteLoadedHint: Stop inference first to delete the loaded model.

aiCfg.title: Bring-your-own AI provider
aiCfg.intro: Optionally store your own AI credentials here so analyses can run on your own account/model — useful when the app-wide AI is disabled by the admin or you prefer a specific provider.
aiCfg.disclaimerBody:
• Cloud providers (Anthropic, OpenAI) charge per request according to their pricing — a large-prompt + reasoning-model analysis can cost €0.05–€1.50 per run.
• Your API key is stored encrypted (AES-128 via Fernet, key derived from the app SECRET_KEY).
• Analysis requests go directly to the provider you choose — we do not forward account data or extra identifiers.
• Under data-protection law you are responsible for picking a provider that meets your requirements (region, DPA, processing).
• Self-hosted endpoints (Ollama, AnythingLLM, open-webui, vLLM, llama.cpp) incur no per-request cost; you carry the hardware load.
aiCfg.providerAnthropicHint: Cloud Claude. Get a key at https://console.anthropic.com.
aiCfg.providerOpenaiHint: Cloud OpenAI. Get a key at https://platform.openai.com. Optional: base URL for Azure OpenAI or compatible cloud proxies.
aiCfg.providerCompatibleHint: Any /v1-compatible server: Ollama, LM Studio, AnythingLLM, open-webui, vLLM, llama.cpp etc. Needs base URL + model; API key often optional/dummy. The reasoning-effort dropdown is hidden here — self-hosted endpoints don't honour the OpenAI parameter; whether a model 'thinks' internally is entirely up to its own architecture.
aiCfg.baseUrlOpenaiHint: Leave empty for OpenAI direct. For Azure OpenAI or proxies: full URL incl. /v1.
aiCfg.baseUrlCompatibleHint: Full URL incl. /v1, e.g. http://myserver:11434/v1 (Ollama) or https://anythingllm.lan/api/v1.
aiCfg.apiKeyEditPlaceholder: Leave empty to keep the stored key — saving will overwrite it completely.
aiCfg.apiKeyHint: Stored encrypted. Always enter the full key when saving.
aiCfg.label: Display label (optional)
aiCfg.reasoningEffortHint: Forces OpenAI's reasoning_effort parameter on supported models. ``high`` ≈ 5–10× more output tokens but visibly deeper coaching findings. Anthropic and most self-hosted servers ignore this.
aiCfg.deleteConfirm: Really remove the stored AI configuration?
aiCfg.errBaseUrlRequired: Base URL is required (full URL with http(s):// and /v1).

legal.privacyIntro: This privacy policy explains, in line with Articles 13 and 14 of the EU General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), how we process personal data when you use this service. We process data only for the purposes described below and only on the legal bases stated.

controller.heading: 1. Controller
controller.body: The controller within the meaning of Article 4 (7) GDPR is the natural person identified in the imprint. Use the email address listed there for any data-protection enquiries.

scope.heading: 2. Scope
scope.body: This policy applies to processing of personal data within this service (the "WoW AI Log Analyzer" web application). It does not apply to external services we link to; those have their own privacy policies.

dataCollected.heading: 3. What we process
dataCollected.body:
We process only the data necessary to operate the service:

• Account data: your email address, your chosen display name, a one-way cryptographic hash of your password (bcrypt — your plaintext password never leaves your browser unencrypted and is never stored), preferred locale, account status.

• Authentication tokens: session and refresh tokens (JWT) stored in your browser to keep you signed in.

• Warcraft Logs connection data (optional): if you connect your WCL account, we store the OAuth access and refresh tokens encrypted with symmetric AES (Fernet), as well as your WCL user ID and display name.

• Report and analysis data: imported Warcraft Logs reports (boss fights, player statistics, casts, buff/debuff uptimes, damage taken, gear) and the AI analyses derived from them. This data describes game characters and is not directly identifying personal data.

• Server logs: when you access the service, the server briefly records technical data (IP address, timestamp, requested resource, user-agent) as is technically necessary for any web application.

purposes.heading: 4. Purposes
purposes.body:
• Operating the application (account, login, locale).
• Importing and storing your WCL reports for local analysis.
• Generating the AI coaching analyses per fight and per player.
• Comparing your performance against cached public top logs for the same spec/encounter.
• Protecting the service from abuse (e.g. rate limiting via server logs).

legalBasis.heading: 5. Legal basis
legalBasis.body:
Processing is based on the following GDPR provisions:
• Art. 6 (1) (b) GDPR (performance of a contract) — for account and report data you provide to use the service.
• Art. 6 (1) (a) GDPR (consent) — for the optional WCL connection and for transmission to an external AI provider, where you actively choose that mode. You can withdraw consent at any time, with effect for the future, by disconnecting or switching back to local mode.
• Art. 6 (1) (f) GDPR (legitimate interest) — for short-term processing of server logs to operate the service securely.

thirdParties.heading: 6. Recipients and transfers
thirdParties.body:
We share data with third parties only in the narrowly limited cases below:

• Warcraft Logs (warcraftlogs.com, operator: Carraway, USA) — when you import a report or connect your account, we query the WCL API. Your request data and, if applicable, OAuth token information is therefore transferred to the United States. Legal basis: contract performance / consent.

• AI providers (only when actively configured) — see section 8.

• Hosting infrastructure — the application runs on a server we operate ourselves within the EU/EEA (see imprint). No transfer to external cloud hosting providers takes place.

wcl.heading: 7. Data retrieval from Warcraft Logs
wcl.body: When you import a report, the service queries the corresponding game events through the official WCL GraphQL API and stores the result in our database. If you connect your WCL account, you can additionally view private and unlisted reports. You can disconnect at any time from your profile; stored tokens are deleted immediately when you do so.

ai.heading: 8. AI analysis of your reports
ai.body:
The actual coaching analysis is generated by a language model. Which provider runs it depends on the configuration of this instance:

• Local (default) — the analysis runs on a locally-hosted model on the same server. No transfer to third parties takes place.

• Anthropic (Claude) or an OpenAI-compatible cloud provider — when enabled, we send the analysis prompt to the chosen provider. We transmit only the game information needed for the analysis (boss, spec, casts, buff uptimes, damage/healing, top-log reference data) and your preferred locale. We do not transmit account data (email, password hash) or any other identifiers. Anthropic processes the data in the United States; an adequate level of protection is ensured via the EU Standard Contractual Clauses. Activating this mode requires your consent.

userApiKeys.heading: 9. Bringing your own AI endpoint (planned feature)
userApiKeys.body: A future version is planned to let you store your own API key for an external AI service (e.g. OpenAI, an Ollama endpoint, or any OpenAI-compatible provider) in your profile. In that case, analysis requests would be sent directly to the provider you choose; the API key would be stored encrypted in our database. Under data-protection law, you would be responsible in that mode for picking a provider that meets your requirements — we would only forward the requests and would not transmit any additional personal data. This feature is not currently active; once it ships we will update this policy accordingly.

captcha.heading: 10. Bot protection on auth forms (Cloudflare Turnstile, optional)
captcha.body:
When enabled on this instance, we protect the sign-in, registration, password-reset and accept-invite forms with Cloudflare Turnstile (provider: Cloudflare, Inc., 101 Townsend St, San Francisco, CA 94107, USA). Turnstile replaces classic captchas and uses technical browser signals to score whether a request is human or automated.

The following data is transmitted to Cloudflare in the process: your IP address, user-agent string, HTTP request headers, a short-lived cookie / local-storage identifier for the verification session, and aggregate browser behaviour signals (e.g. mouse / keyboard activity). We do not set persistent identifying cookies ourselves; Cloudflare sets short-lived cookies of its own for the verification (typical lifetime 30 min.).

Legal basis is Art. 6 (1) (f) GDPR (legitimate interest in protecting our auth endpoints from automated abuse). The transfer to the United States is covered by the EU Standard Contractual Clauses Cloudflare has executed with its group entities. For details see Cloudflare's privacy policy at https://www.cloudflare.com/privacypolicy/ and the supplementary notes for Turnstile at https://www.cloudflare.com/application-services/products/turnstile/.

If Turnstile is not enabled on this instance (the default), this processing does not occur.

retention.heading: 11. Retention
retention.body:
• Account data: as long as your account is active. When the account is deleted, all associated data (reports, analyses, WCL tokens) is automatically removed via cascading deletes.
• Imported reports and analyses: until you delete them yourself or remove your account.
• Cached top logs: up to 90 days; they are automatically replaced by new refreshes.
• Server logs: at most 14 days, for security and diagnostics.

cookies.heading: 12. Cookies, local storage
cookies.body: We do not set tracking cookies or advertising cookies. Your browser's local storage holds only technically necessary data: your session tokens (JWT) and a cached copy of your profile so the sign-in experience stays smooth. You can clear this data at any time by signing out or wiping your browser storage.

rights.heading: 13. Your rights
rights.body:
Under the GDPR you have, in particular, the following rights:
• Right of access (Art. 15)
• Right to rectification (Art. 16)
• Right to erasure / "right to be forgotten" (Art. 17)
• Right to restriction of processing (Art. 18)
• Right to data portability (Art. 20)
• Right to object to processing based on Art. 6 (1) (f) (Art. 21)
• Right to withdraw consent given, with effect for the future (Art. 7 (3))

You can exercise these rights via the contact email address listed in the imprint. You can also delete your account directly from your profile.

complaint.heading: 14. Right to lodge a complaint
complaint.body: You have the right to lodge a complaint with a data-protection supervisory authority if you believe that the processing of your data infringes the GDPR. The competent authority is in particular the supervisory authority of the federal state in which the controller is based. A list of all German supervisory authorities is available at https://www.bfdi.bund.de/.

changes.heading: 15. Changes to this policy
changes.body: We reserve the right to update this policy in response to material changes to the service (e.g. new features, provider changes). The current version is always available via the footer of this application; the date at the top reflects the most recent revision.
